subject: Horizon Health — clarification on transfer safeguards, SCCs and UK addendum
messages:
From: James Owen <james.owen@horizonhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA + TIA scope — quick clarifications

Hi Stephanie / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attaching our DPA draft and a very high-level TIA scope sheet. Before we move to our procurement team and DocuSign we have two quick asks we hoped you could confirm: 

1) For EU customer data, are you proposing standard SCCs plus the UK IDTA where applicable, or do you intend to rely on the EU SCCs alone and use the UK addendum only for UK-resident accounts? We need a clear line for our legal team.

2) Assume Horizon will request a subprocessor list and 30-day notification for new subprocessors — will Redwood provide a retrieval API for the list or just scheduled exports? A programmatic option would be ideal for our infra team.

I've attached Horizon_DPA_draft_v1.pdf and Horizon_TIA_Scope.xlsx. Can you confirm whether Redwood needs a signed DPA + UK addendum or a single combined signature?

Appreciate a short email reply. We need to close this by end of next week to meet our vendor onboarding window.

Best,
James Owen
Head of Vendor Risk
Horizon Health

Attachments: Horizon_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (pdf), Horizon_TIA_Scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: James Owen <james.owen@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + TIA scope — quick clarifications

James — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Short answers up top, details below:

- We support EU SCCs as the baseline; for UK data we apply the UK IDTA (UK addendum) when Horizon designates UK-resident accounts in the onboarding metadata. In practice that means both documents will be in our execution bundle for customers operating in both jurisdictions.
- Subprocessor list: we offer both a scheduled export and a small API endpoint (GET /v1/subprocessors) that returns current subprocessors and their regions. The API can be polled; we also push notifications for changes and we can add Horizon to a targeted webhook.
- Execution flow: Redwood prefers a single DPA execution with annexes for TIA/SCC/UK Addendum so there's one signature packet. We can produce a combined DocuSign flow (DPA + Annex A: SCCs + Annex B: UK IDTA when applicable).

Details / follow-ups:
1) SCC / UK addendum decision logic
  - If Horizon flags an account country = UK during signup, we add the UK IDTA to the contract binder and surface that to legal and billing.
  - If the account processes mixed EU/UK data, both SCCs and the UK addendum will be included; our legal team handles precedence language in Annexes.

2) TIA scoping
  - Naomi (copied) is our transfer-safeguards lead; she can walk through the TIA template and the mapping to subprocessors / regional routing.

3) Next steps
  - Can you confirm (a) whether Horizon wants webhook notifications for subprocessor additions and (b) whether the onboarding team will accept the combined execution packet?

I can draft a short note for procurement summarizing the flow if that helps accelerate sign-off.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: James Owen <james.owen@horizonhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + TIA scope — quick clarifications

Thanks James — quick technical notes from infra/ops side: 

- The GET /v1/subprocessors endpoint is live in our sandbox and returns JSON with names, regions, data categories, and last-updated timestamp. We can add an additional field \"notification_url_subscribed\" if Horizon wants to manage subscriptions programmatically.
- For the TIA, the Horizon_TIA_Scope.xlsx looks mostly aligned; one ask: please add an example dataset sample or a single row describing an expected PII flow (source system, retention, intended processing) — that helps us size fallback encryption and caching controls.

Also noting that Route/Cache controls for EU traffic will default to our eu-central-1 cluster unless you request an onshore-only footprint. If Horizon needs onshore-only (UK-only) processing for given namespaces, that is doable under Private deployments or an enterprise routing add-on.

If you want I can spin up the sandbox endpoint and share credentials for Horizon's infra team for validation.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

From: James Owen <james.owen@horizonhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@horizonhealth.com>, Horizon Health Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + TIA scope — quick clarifications

On Mon, Jul 15, 2028 at 11:03 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> James — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Short answers up top, details below:
>
> - We support EU SCCs as the baseline; for UK data we apply the UK IDTA (UK addendum) when Horizon designates UK-resident accounts in the onboarding metadata. In practice that means both documents will be in our execution bundle for customers operating in both jurisdictions.

Thanks — that matches our expectations. Two additional follow-ups from legal: 

1) Can Redwood confirm whether subprocessors that only touch non-personal-data telemetry (healthchecks, metrics) will be excluded from the TIA scope, or should we list them and mark category = "non-personal"? Horizon legal prefers a minimalist TIA list but will accept classification flags.

2) For the UK addendum, can you provide a short paragraph describing fallback jurisdictional assurances (i.e., how do you preserve access controls and logging when requests route across EU/UK under transient routing)?

We should be able to get procurement to accept a combined DocuSign packet if you provide the little paragraph and the subprocessor classification guidance. I can attach a short procurement checklist to the DocuSign envelope.

-James

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: James Owen <james.owen@horizonhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + TIA scope — quick clarifications

James / team — following up with the two items requested. Below is language you can paste into the procurement checklist / DocuSign cover note, plus guidance on subprocessor classification.

1) Subprocessor classification guidance
- Include any third party that processes Customer Personal Data in the TIA.
- Telemetry-only vendors (metrics, availability monitoring) should be included if they have access to or could reconstruct personal identifiers. If they process only aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry we recommend listing them under \"Operational Telemetry — non-personal\" with category flag = \"non-personal\" and sample datapoint example.

2) UK addendum / fallback routing paragraph (for procurement packet):
\"Redwood Inference executes the EU SCCs as the contractual baseline. For UK-resident accounts, the UK IDTA will be appended as an addendum. When transient routing between EU and UK infrastructure occurs, Redwood enforces consistent access controls (RBAC + short-lived credentials), retains request-level audit logs in the account-specific logging partition, and applies the same encryption-at-rest and key custody policies across regions. Where regulatory requirements mandate UK-only processing, Redwood offers onshore-only routing options or a Private deployment; these options are documented in Annex C (Routing Options) and are available through our Sales/Support team.\"

3) Next steps
- Stephanie: if that paragraph looks good to you I'll ask Legal to produce the annex text for the combined DPA packet.
- James: if Horizon wants webhook notifications for subprocessor additions, Kimberly's team can enable a test subscription and Naomi will confirm the exact JSON schema.

Laura, can you add the paragraph above into a one-page procurement summary and we'll send a combined DocuSign packet once James confirms?

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy & Transfer Safeguards Lead
Redwood Inference

James — attaching a one-page procurement summary and the proposed DocuSign flow for the combined packet. Key bullets for your procurement checklist: 
- Execution: Single DPA with Annex A (EU SCCs) and Annex B (UK IDTA) appended conditionally.
- Subprocessor list: API + export available; webhook optional (recommended cadence: immediate change notifications, weekly digest).
- Routing: Default eu-central-1 for EU; UK IDTA triggers UK routing policies and flags for onshore-only needs.
- Evidence: audit logs retained for 12 months by default; extended retention available on request.

If this looks good I will create the DocuSign envelope (DPA + Annexes + checklist) and share the link.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — Laura
Laura Bennett
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
